701150.t: From Proto-Hellenic *anḗr, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂nḗr. Cognates include Sanskrit नृ (nṛ́), नर॑ (nára), Latin neriosus and Old Irish nert.

701137.t: Unknown. Maybe from Proto-Indo-European *sń̥h₂u or *sn̥h₂eu, which could be derived from a more primary particle *sń̥ (“separated, without”) or the locative of some (hard-to-identify) noun.

701163.t: First attested in Hellenic as Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀵𐀫𐀦 (a-to-ro-qo), of uncertain origin. Scholars used to consider it to be a compound from ἀνήρ (ănḗr, “man”) and ὤψ (ṓps, “face, appearance, look”): thus, "he who looks like a man".

701160.t: Disputed. * Possibly from a Mediterranean substrate; compare Old Armenian անթայր (antʻayr, “spark; anthrax”), անթեղ (antʻeł, “hot coal, ember”).

701157.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ántʰos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éndʰos. Cognate with Vedic Sanskrit अन्धस् (ándhas, “Soma, grass, herb”), Albanian endë, Old Armenian անդ (and, “field”), possibly Old Frisian åndul.

701123.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ánemos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂enh₁mos, a nominal derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₂enh₁- (“breathe”).

701100.t: From ἀνδρεῖος (andreîos, “manly”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun–forming suffix). Compare ἠνορέη (ēnoréē).

701110.t: From ἀνδρο- (andro-, “man”) + θείνω (theínō, “to slay”) + -ος (-os). Cognate to Sanskrit नृहन् (nṛhán, nṛghné).

701194.t: From ἀ- (a-, without) + νόμος (nómos, “law, ordinance; melody”).

701113.t: From ἀνα- (ana-, “an intensifying prefix”) + ἐγείρω (egeírō, “to wake”)

701184.t: From ἀ- (a-, “without”) + νοέω (noéō, “to perceive”) + -τός (-tós, adjectival suffix).
